Lina: Quick pulse — heads up: canary signals on eu-west started spiking for v3.9.2 about 20m ago. Seeing tail latency + error rate on embed endpoints. @Sam can you confirm?
Ben: I saw the alert, looks like a small surge from a single client TTL test. Error % up ~4% on pods rtx-2, rtx-3.
Marta: Noted. Rolling canary is at 10% traffic. Should we hold the train and extend the freeze window? :thinking_face:
Sam: Confirmed, reproduces locally with a long prompt pattern that causes KV cache pressure. Investigating whether batching thresholds are misfiring.
Lina: Decision time: hold canary for 1h and throttle new deploys. If we can mitigate without rollback, we resume. Otherwise roll back to v3.9.1.
deploy-bot: Automated action — canary traffic reduced to 2%. Autoscale:min=2,max=6 enforced. (action id: dpl-1749987654)
Ben: Quick mitigation idea: lower continuous-batch-size from 128->64 for the embeddings route, disable prefix-cache for affected pods, and bump kernel-retry timeout to 60s. Patch is low-risk.
Marta: Can you draft the patch? I can apply and run canary smoke.
Sam: Patch ready in PR: https://git.redwood/example/patch/314 — includes config toggle and telemetry markers. Running smoke now.
Ava: Smoke results: latency back to baseline, error rate dropped to 0.5% on test traffic. Telemetry shows reduced KV miss churn.
Lina: OK good. Action items: 1) Ben to patch prod config toggle and monitor for 30m. 2) Product to notify the affected customer (SLA note). 3) Release train: freeze extended by 1 hour — no new canaries until 1749993820.
Ben: Applying patch now. Will post status in 10m.
Sam: Added a short-term alert: KV-cache-miss-rate > 1% for 5m triggers pager.
Marta: Noted. Also let's add a follow-up to eng-releases retro: investigate batching heuristics and add unit test for prompt-length distributions.
Lina: Thanks all. If nothing regresses, we'll resume the train at the new window and proceed with the rest of the queued rollouts. :thumbsup:
